about.ex: The report is about a data breach.

account.en: an arrangement to keep money in a bank
account.ex: She opened a savings account last year.

accounts.en: an arrangement to keep money in a bank

acquired.ex: The firm acquired a small software company.

addressing.ex: We must start addressing the cause of the delays.

advised.en: told someone what they should do
advised.ex: The doctor advised him to rest for a week.

affect.en: to change or have an effect on
affect.ex: The strike will affect thousands of travellers.

affected.ex: Many homes were affected by the flood.

affecting.en: having an influence or effect on
affecting.ex: The new rule is affecting many small shops.

alarm.ex: The news caused alarm among parents.

alerted.ex: A neighbour alerted the police to the smoke.

allay.en: to make a fear or worry smaller
allay.ex: The doctor tried to allay her fears.

example.en: The minister tried to allay public fears.
example.zh: 部長試圖平息民眾的恐懼。

note.meaning: 平息、減輕（恐懼、憂慮、疑慮）。
note.usage: 幾乎只接 fears/concerns/anxiety/suspicion，屬正式用語。

noteEn.meaning: to make fears or worries smaller.

noteEs.exampleTr: El ministro intentó disipar los temores del público.
noteEs.meaning: calmar o disipar miedos o preocupaciones.

noteHi.exampleTr: मंत्री ने लोगों का डर कम करने की कोशिश की।
noteHi.usage: लगभग हमेशा fears/concerns/anxiety के साथ; औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 大臣は国民の不安を和らげようとした。
noteJa.meaning: 不安や懸念を和らげる。
noteJa.usage: fears/concerns/anxiety と共に使う正式な語。

noteKo.usage: 거의 항상 fears/concerns/anxiety와 함께 쓰는 격식어.

among.en: including; as part of a group

anxiety.ex: Exams cause anxiety for many students.

appear.ex: The message may appear to come from your bank.

approximately.en: close to a number, not exact
approximately.ex: The trip takes approximately three hours.

are.ex: The shops are open until six.

arguably.ex: She is arguably the best player in the team.
arguably.ja: おそらく；ほぼ間違いなく

armed.ex: Armed with a map, we set off into the hills.

assessment.ex: The safety assessment took six months.

assurances.en: promises that something is true or will happen
assurances.ex: We received assurances that the work would finish soon.

assured.en: told someone firmly that something is true
assured.ex: The pilot assured us the flight would be safe.

at.en: in a place, time or level

authentic.ex: The museum says the painting is authentic.

aware.ex: She was aware of the danger.

balances.en: the money left in a bank account
balances.ex: Check your bank balance before you shop.

bank.en: a business that keeps and lends money
bank.ex: She opened an account at the bank.

banking.ex: She has worked in banking for ten years.

based.ex: The firm is based in Galway.

be.en: exist; also used to form passives
be.ex: The meeting will be on Monday.

been.ex: The road has been closed all week.

began.ex: The concert began at eight o'clock.

belfast.zh: 貝爾法斯特（北愛爾蘭首府）

belfast-based.en: with its main office in Belfast
belfast-based.ja: ベルファストに拠点を置く
belfast-based.zh: 總部位於貝爾法斯特的

believed.ex: She believed the plan would work.

branded.ex: Critics branded the plan a failure.

breach.en: a break in security that lets data be stolen
breach.ex: The company reported a breach of customer data.

example.en: The bank apologised for the data breach.
example.zh: 銀行為資料外洩事件道歉。

note.meaning: （安全或資料的）外洩、破口；也可作動詞「違反」。
note.usage: data/security breach 為資安常用語；動詞 breach rules/a contract 表「違反」。

noteEn.meaning: a break in security that lets information be stolen.
noteEn.usage: Common: 'data breach', 'security breach'. As a verb: 'breach the rules'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El banco pidió disculpas por la filtración de datos.
noteEs.usage: data/security breach; como verbo, breach rules = incumplir normas.

noteHi.exampleTr: बैंक ने डेटा सेंधमारी के लिए माफ़ी माँगी।
noteHi.usage: data/security breach आम है; क्रिया के रूप में breach rules = नियम तोड़ना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 銀行はデータ流出について謝罪した。
noteJa.meaning: セキュリティの侵害；情報流出。
noteJa.usage: data/security breach の形が多い。動詞 breach rules は「違反する」。

noteKo.usage: data/security breach 형태가 흔하다. 동사 breach rules는 ‘위반하다’.

briefed.ex: The officer briefed the team before the visit.

called.ex: The new park is called Green Hill.

caught.en: caught up in = involved in something unwanted
caught.ex: Many travellers were caught up in the strike.
caught.ja: 巻き込まれた（caught up in）

central.en: main; Central Bank: the national bank
central.ex: The central bank sets interest rates.

certain.ex: Certain shops close early on Sundays.

characterised.en: described something in a particular way
characterised.ex: Critics characterised the plan as unfair.

clarification.en: an explanation that makes something clear
clarification.ex: I asked my manager for clarification on the new rule.

clients.en: people or firms who pay for a service
clients.ex: The lawyer meets new clients on Mondays.

commission.en: an official group with a special job
commission.ex: The commission will publish its report next week.

communicate.ex: Teachers communicate with parents by email.

communications.en: messages sent by email, text or post
communications.ex: All communications from the bank are in English.

company's.ex: The company's profits fell last year.

comprehensive.ex: The guide gives a comprehensive list of courses.

compromised.en: harmed or made unsafe by an attack
compromised.ex: The email account was compromised last night.

example.en: The hospital said no patient data was compromised.
example.zh: 醫院表示沒有病患資料外洩。

note.meaning: （資料、系統、安全）遭到入侵、洩露或受損。
note.usage: 資訊安全常用被動式：data/security/an account was compromised；另有「妥協」之意，需看語境。

noteEn.meaning: accessed, damaged or exposed by an attacker.
noteEn.usage: Often passive in security: 'data was compromised'. It can also mean 'agree to give up something'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El hospital dijo que no se vieron comprometidos datos de pacientes.
noteEs.meaning: que los datos o un sistema han sido vulnerados o expuestos.
noteEs.usage: En ciberseguridad suele ir en pasiva: data was compromised; también significa ceder en un acuerdo.

noteHi.exampleTr: अस्पताल ने कहा कि किसी मरीज़ का डेटा लीक नहीं हुआ।
noteHi.meaning: डेटा या सिस्टम में सेंध लगना या उसकी सुरक्षा भंग होना।
noteHi.usage: साइबर सुरक्षा में प्रायः passive: data was compromised; 'समझौता करना' का अर्थ भी होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 病院は患者のデータは漏洩していないと述べた。
noteJa.meaning: データやシステムが侵害・漏洩されること。
noteJa.usage: 情報セキュリティでは受動態が多い：data was compromised。「妥協する」の意味もあるので文脈に注意。

noteKo.exampleTr: 병원은 환자 데이터가 유출되지 않았다고 밝혔다.
noteKo.usage: 보안 분야에서는 수동태가 흔하다: data was compromised; '타협하다'라는 뜻도 있다.

computer.en: an electronic machine for working with information
computer.ex: I use my computer for school work.

concern.ex: There is growing concern about rents.

concerning.ex: The latest figures are very concerning.

confirmed.en: shown to be true by tests
confirmed.ex: The results were confirmed by the lab.

consequently.ex: He missed the bus and consequently arrived late.

example.en: Rents rose; consequently, many families moved away.
example.zh: 租金上漲，因此許多家庭搬走了。

note.usage: 連接副詞，表示前因後果，常放句首加逗號，比 so 正式。

noteEn.usage: A formal linking word; often starts a sentence: 'Consequently, ...'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los alquileres subieron; por consiguiente, muchas familias se mudaron.
noteEs.usage: Conector formal de causa-efecto, más formal que so; suele ir al inicio con coma.

noteHi.exampleTr: किराया बढ़ा; परिणामस्वरूप कई परिवार चले गए।
noteHi.usage: कारण-परिणाम दिखाने वाला औपचारिक शब्द; so से अधिक औपचारिक, अक्सर वाक्य की शुरुआत में।

noteJa.exampleTr: 家賃が上がり、その結果多くの家族が引っ越した。
noteJa.usage: 因果関係を示す接続副詞で、so より硬い。文頭でカンマと共に使うことが多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 임대료가 올랐고, 그 결과 많은 가족이 이사했다.
noteKo.usage: 인과 관계를 나타내는 접속 부사로 so보다 격식 있음; 주로 문두에 쉼표와 함께.

considerable.ex: The project took a considerable amount of time.

constellation.en: part of the company name Constellation Software
constellation.ja: コンステレーション（社名）

consult.ex: Consult the map before you leave.

contact.ex: Call the contact centre for help.

contacted.ex: I contacted the company by email.

contain.en: to have something inside or as part

contingent.ex: The deal is contingent upon funding.

example.en: The offer is contingent upon a good report.
example.zh: 這份錄取取決於一份良好的報告。

note.usage: 固定搭配 be contingent upon/on sth，等於 depend on，屬正式用法。

noteEs.exampleTr: La oferta está supeditada a un buen informe.

noteHi.exampleTr: यह प्रस्ताव अच्छी रिपोर्ट पर निर्भर है।

noteJa.exampleTr: その申し出は良い報告次第だ。
noteJa.usage: be contingent upon/on 〜 は depend on の硬い言い方。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 제안은 좋은 보고서에 달려 있다.

continuing.ex: Prices are continuing to rise this year.

convincing.ex: He gave a convincing excuse for being late.
convincing.ja: もっともらしい；説得力のある

coordinating.en: working together in an organised way
coordinating.ex: Police are coordinating with fire crews at the scene.

copy.en: to make the same thing again
copy.ex: Please copy the file to your laptop.

core.ex: Trust is at the core of any team.

country.en: a nation with its own government

craft.en: to make something carefully and with skill
craft.ex: She crafted a short speech for the wedding.

credentials.en: login details such as usernames and passwords
credentials.ex: Never share your login credentials with anyone.

credible.en: able to be believed or trusted
credible.ex: The police found no credible evidence.

example.en: The newspaper relied on a credible source.
example.zh: 這家報紙引用了可信的消息來源。

note.usage: 常修飾 evidence, claim, source；反義 incredible 意思不同，宜用 not credible。

noteEs.exampleTr: El periódico se basó en una fuente fiable.

noteHi.exampleTr: अख़बार ने एक विश्वसनीय स्रोत पर भरोसा किया।

noteJa.exampleTr: その新聞は信頼できる情報源に基づいた。
noteJa.meaning: 信頼できる；信用に足る。
noteJa.usage: evidence, claim, source などを修飾。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 신문은 믿을 만한 소식통에 의존했다.

credit.en: credit union: a bank owned by its members
credit.ex: Many farmers save with a local credit union.

customers.en: people or groups who buy a service
customers.ex: The shop gave customers a small discount.

cyber.en: related to computers and the internet
cyber.ex: Cyber attacks on banks are rising.

danger.ex: The old bridge is a danger to drivers.

data.en: facts and numbers collected for study
data.ex: The app collects data about your sleep.

deeply.ex: She was deeply moved by the story.

department.ex: The Department of Education sets the rules.

described.ex: She described the trip as amazing.

designed.ex: The course is designed for beginners.

details.ex: Fill in your personal details here.

directly.ex: The money goes directly to the school.

disclose.ex: Companies must disclose their profits every year.

example.en: Companies must disclose all fees before payment.
example.zh: 公司必須在付款前公開所有費用。

note.usage: disclose + 資訊 (to sb)；名詞 disclosure；比 tell/show 更正式。

noteEs.exampleTr: Las empresas deben revelar todas las tarifas antes del pago.

noteHi.exampleTr: कंपनियों को भुगतान से पहले सभी शुल्क बताने होंगे।

noteJa.exampleTr: 企業は支払い前にすべての手数料を開示しなければならない。
noteJa.usage: disclose 情報 (to 人)。名詞は disclosure。

noteKo.exampleTr: 기업은 결제 전에 모든 수수료를 공개해야 한다.

dupe.en: to trick someone into believing something false
dupe.ex: The scammers duped him into paying a fake bill.

earlier.ex: She had called earlier that day.

echoed.en: repeated or agreed with what someone else said
echoed.ex: The mayor echoed calls for better buses.

eliminated.ex: The disease was eliminated from the country years ago.

emails.ex: I get many emails every day.

encouraged.en: asked and gave support to do something
encouraged.ex: The teacher encouraged us to read more.

episode.en: a single event or period of time
episode.ex: The episode taught us to be careful.

exploited.en: used a weakness for a bad purpose
exploited.ex: The thieves exploited a gap in the fence.

example.en: Scammers exploited a gap in the booking system.
example.zh: 詐騙者利用了訂票系統的漏洞。

note.meaning: 利用（弱點、漏洞）以謀取不當利益；也可指「剝削」。
note.usage: exploit a weakness/loophole/vulnerability；被動 be exploited 可指勞工被剝削。

noteEn.meaning: used a weakness unfairly for gain.
noteEn.usage: 'exploit a weakness/loophole'; 'be exploited' can mean treated unfairly.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los estafadores aprovecharon un fallo del sistema de reservas.
noteEs.meaning: aprovechar una debilidad de forma abusiva; explotar.
noteEs.usage: exploit a weakness/loophole; be exploited = ser explotado.

noteHi.exampleTr: धोखेबाज़ों ने बुकिंग सिस्टम की खामी का फ़ायदा उठाया।
noteHi.meaning: कमज़ोरी का गलत फ़ायदा उठाना; शोषण करना।
noteHi.usage: exploit a weakness/loophole; be exploited = शोषण होना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 詐欺師は予約システムの欠陥を悪用した。
noteJa.meaning: 弱点を悪用する；搾取する。
noteJa.usage: exploit a weakness/loophole の形。受け身 be exploited は「搾取される」。

noteKo.usage: exploit a weakness/loophole 형태. 수동태 be exploited는 ‘착취당하다’.

expressed.ex: Parents expressed concern about the plan.

extract.en: to take out information or material
extract.ex: The app can extract text from photos.

fake.ex: He paid with a fake note.

fallen.en: fallen into: come under the control of
fallen.ex: The plans had fallen into the wrong hands.

fallout.en: the bad results of an event
fallout.ex: The fallout from the scandal lasted months.

fears.en: worries that something bad may happen
fears.ex: Fears of a strike grew last week.

finance.en: money matters managed by a government
finance.zh: 財政（Minister for Finance：財政部長）

firm.ex: He works for a small law firm.

fixed.ex: The bug was fixed in the latest update.

flaw.en: a mistake or weak part in something
flaw.ex: Engineers found a flaw in the design.

for.en: intended to belong to or help

found.ex: The virus was found in two cows.

fraudsters.en: people who trick others to get money

fraudulent.en: based on lies to get money
fraudulent.ex: The bank stopped several fraudulent payments.

further.ex: A further ten jobs will be created.

genuine.ex: She showed genuine interest in the students' ideas.

hackers.en: people who break into computer systems

had.ex: She had a good idea for the festival.

half.ex: More than half of people agreed.

handing.ex: They are handing over half their pay.

hands.en: fall into the wrong hands: be taken by bad people
hands.ex: The keys must not fall into the wrong hands.
hands.zh: 手中（fall into criminal hands：落入犯罪者手中）

has.en: owns; also used to form perfect tenses

have.en: own; also used to form perfect tenses

held.ex: The files are held on a secure server.

house.en: software house: a company that makes software
house.ex: She joined a small software house in Cork.

however.ex: It was cold; however, we went for a walk.

incident.en: an event, often a problem like an attack
incident.ex: The bank reported the incident to the police.

include.ex: The price does not include breakfast.

including.en: and also; as part of the total
including.ex: Ten people came, including my aunt.

increasing.ex: The company is increasing its staff.

individually.ex: The teacher spoke to each student individually.

inquiry.ex: An inquiry into the accident has begun.

insidious.en: harmful in a slow or hidden way
insidious.ex: Loneliness can have an insidious effect on health.
insidious.ja: 潜行性の；じわじわ害を及ぼす

institutions.ex: EU institutions are based in Brussels.

intruders.en: people who enter a place or system illegally
intruders.ex: The alarm scared the intruders away.

investigating.en: examining something carefully to find facts
investigating.ex: Investigating the old mine took several months.

investigation.en: an official careful study of facts
investigation.ex: Police started an investigation into the fire.

involving.en: including or having as a part
involving.ex: There were three accidents involving buses.

irish.en: from Ireland (The Irish Times: 報紙名)

it.en: it: that thing; IT: information technology

known.ex: The tests are known as dissolution tests.

league.en: a group of organisations that work together
league.zh: 聯盟（Irish League of Credit Unions：愛爾蘭信用合作社聯盟）

leaving.ex: Check every payment leaving your account.

left.ex: Money left my account twice by mistake.

liaising.en: talking and working with another group
liaising.ex: The school is liaising with parents about the trip.

lies.ex: The answer lies in better training.

likely.ex: It is likely to rain later.

look.ex: The fake website looks very real.

loophole.en: a gap or weakness that lets people get around rules or security
loophole.ex: The new law closes a tax loophole.

magnifies.en: makes something bigger or more serious

example.en: Poor planning magnifies the risk of delays.
example.zh: 規劃不良會放大延誤的風險。

note.meaning: 放大；使（問題、風險）更嚴重。
note.usage: 常接 risk, problem, effect, impact；比 increase 更強調「放大效應」。

noteEn.meaning: makes something bigger or more serious.

noteEs.exampleTr: Una mala planificación amplifica el riesgo de retrasos.
noteEs.meaning: amplificar; agravar un problema o riesgo.
noteEs.usage: Con risk, problem, impact; más expresivo que increase.

noteHi.exampleTr: खराब योजना देरी का जोखिम बढ़ा देती है।
noteHi.meaning: बढ़ा देना; समस्या को और गंभीर बनाना।
noteHi.usage: risk, problem, impact के साथ आता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 計画が不十分だと遅れのリスクが拡大する。
noteJa.meaning: 拡大する；問題を深刻にする。
noteJa.usage: risk, problem, impact などと結びつく。

main.ex: The main station is in the city centre.

makes.ex: This company makes phones and laptops.

many.ex: Many people work from home now.

matter.en: a case or subject being dealt with
matter.ex: The matter will be discussed next week.

member.ex: Every member of the team helped.

members.en: people who belong to a group

messages.en: ideas or information people want to communicate
messages.ex: We see many advertising messages every day.

million.ex: The city has over one million people.

minister.en: a member of the government who leads a department
minister.ex: The minister visited the new hospital.

misgivings.ex: She had misgivings about the deal.

money.en: what you use to buy things
money.ex: They need money for the repairs.

most.ex: This is the most recent version.

necessary.ex: Is it necessary to book a table?

needed.ex: More teachers are needed in rural areas.

neither.en: not one and not the other

nevertheless.ex: It was cold; nevertheless, many came.

example.en: The cost is high; nevertheless, the project will go ahead.
example.zh: 成本很高，然而計畫仍將進行。

note.usage: 表轉折，常放句首加逗號，語氣比 however 更強調讓步。

noteEn.usage: Often at the start of a sentence, followed by a comma.

noteEs.exampleTr: El coste es alto; no obstante, el proyecto seguirá adelante.
noteEs.usage: Indica contraste; suele ir al inicio con coma.

noteHi.exampleTr: लागत ऊँची है; फिर भी परियोजना आगे बढ़ेगी।
noteHi.usage: विरोध दिखाने के लिए, अक्सर वाक्य के शुरू में।

noteJa.exampleTr: 費用は高いが、それでも計画は進められる。
noteJa.meaning: それにもかかわらず；しかし。
noteJa.usage: 逆接を表し、文頭にコンマ付きで置くことが多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 비용이 높지만 그럼에도 사업은 진행될 것이다.
noteKo.usage: 대조를 나타내며 문장 앞에 쉼표와 함께 쓴다.

not.ex: The shop is not open today.

notably.ex: Notably, prices fell in rural areas.

notifications.en: official messages telling someone about something
notifications.ex: The council sent notifications to all residents.

notified.ex: We notified the police at once.

off.ex: Criminals tried to siphon off money from the charity.

on.ex: She wrote a report on the data breach.

order.en: in order to: so that you can
order.ex: She saved money in order to buy a car.

out.ex: The school will reach out to every family.

outgoing.ex: Check your outgoing payments every month.

over.ex: Over half of the students passed.

own.en: belonging to that person or group
own.ex: They want to run their own business.

owned.ex: The shop is owned by two sisters.

passwords.en: secret words used to log in
passwords.ex: Change your passwords every few months.

people.ex: Many people came to the event.

phishing.en: tricking people online to get their passwords or bank details
phishing.ex: Do not click links in phishing emails.

platform.en: a computer system that runs services
platform.ex: The new platform lets customers pay online.

plausible.en: seeming reasonable and likely to be true
plausible.ex: Her story sounded plausible to the police.

point.en: weak point: a part that can be easily attacked
point.ex: The old door was the weak point in the house.

potentially.ex: The change could potentially save money.
potentially.ja: 潜在的に；〜する可能性がある

priority.zh: 優先事項（top priority：首要任務）

probability.en: how likely something is to happen
probability.ex: The probability of a storm this week is high.

prompted.ex: The storm prompted the school to close early.

protection.ex: The law gives protection to online shoppers.
protection.zh: 保護（Data Protection Commission：資料保護委員會）

provider.en: a company that supplies a service
provider.ex: We changed our internet provider last month.

provider's.en: belonging to the company that provides the service

paragraphs: Hackers may have taken personal data from 43 credit unions in Ireland. A credit union is a small local bank. Its customers are called members.
The problem started at a computer company in Belfast. The company is called Wellington IT. It makes software for many credit unions.
The hackers found a weak point in the software. They took some member records. These include details of payments from accounts.
Up to 1.8 million people could be affected. That is more than half of all members in Ireland.
The credit unions say no money was taken. Account balances are safe. The weak point is now closed.

But criminals could use the stolen data to send fake emails or texts. Simon Harris, the Minister for Finance, said the news was very worrying. Members should talk to their credit union if they are worried.

paragraphs: Personal information about members of 43 credit unions in Ireland may have been stolen by hackers. Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris said the news was deeply worrying.

The problem began at Wellington IT, a software company based in Belfast. It provides the banking system used by more than a third of Irish credit unions. The company contacted the affected credit unions earlier this week.

It is believed that the hackers used a weakness in the company's software to copy some member records. These records include details of payments that left people's accounts. Up to 1.8 million people could be affected, which is more than half of all credit union members in the country.

The Irish League of Credit Unions said it knew about a security problem at a service provider. It said the weakness had now been fixed and that accounts and balances were safe. The company is still investigating what happened.
The main danger is that criminals could use the stolen information to send fake messages, a trick known as phishing. These messages may look real because they contain true personal details.

The Data Protection Commission has received several reports from credit unions. The Department of Finance is also talking to the Central Bank. Credit unions will contact members directly if needed, and Minister of State Robert Troy told worried members to speak to their credit union.

paragraphs: A suspected data breach at 43 credit unions could affect hundreds of thousands of members across Ireland. Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris described the incident as deeply concerning.

The affected credit unions were contacted earlier this week by Wellington IT, a Belfast-based software provider. Founded in 1983 and owned since 2014 by the Canadian firm Constellation Software, it supplies the banking platform for more than a third of Irish credit unions.

Hackers are understood to have exploited a vulnerability in the company's software to extract some member records, including details of payments leaving accounts. As many as 1.8 million people, more than half of all credit union members in the State, could potentially be affected.

The Irish League of Credit Unions confirmed it was aware of an IT security incident at a service provider. It said it had been assured that the vulnerability was closed and that accounts and balances had not been compromised, although the provider's investigation is continuing.
The greatest risk is that the stolen data could be used for targeted phishing, where criminals send convincing messages designed to trick people into revealing passwords or bank details.

The Data Protection Commission said it had received several breach notifications and was treating the matter as a priority. The Department of Finance is in contact with the Central Bank, which is also aware of the incident.
Credit unions will contact members directly where necessary. Minister of State Robert Troy also expressed concern and urged anyone worried to speak to their credit union.

paragraphs: A suspected cyber breach affecting 43 credit unions has raised fears that the personal data of vast numbers of members may have fallen into criminal hands. Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris branded the episode deeply concerning.

The alarm was raised earlier this week when Wellington IT, a Belfast software house, alerted its clients. The firm, established in 1983 and acquired by Canada's Constellation Software in 2014, underpins the core banking systems of over a third of the country's credit unions.

Intruders are believed to have exploited a flaw in its software to siphon off member records, among them details of outgoing payments. The potential fallout is considerable: up to 1.8 million people, or more than half of the sector's membership, could be caught up in the incident.

Seeking to allay anxiety, the Irish League of Credit Unions said it had been assured that the loophole was now sealed and that neither accounts nor balances had been compromised. The provider's inquiry, however, remains ongoing.

The more insidious threat lies in phishing. Armed with genuine personal details, fraudsters could craft highly plausible messages that dupe recipients into handing over passwords or banking credentials.

The Data Protection Commission confirmed it had been notified by several credit unions and was pursuing the matter urgently, while the Department of Finance is liaising with the Central Bank, which has also been briefed.

Credit unions are to reach out to members individually where warranted. Minister of State Robert Troy echoed the Government's unease and encouraged anyone with misgivings to consult their credit union.

paragraphs: A suspected data breach involving 43 credit unions has prompted substantial concern regarding the security of personal information held by Ireland's financial institutions. Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris characterised the incident as deeply concerning.

The breach originated at Wellington IT, a Belfast-based software provider established in 1983 and subsequently acquired by the Canadian company Constellation Software in 2014. Notably, the firm supplies the banking platform for more than a third of Irish credit unions, which consequently magnifies the potential scale of the incident.

It is understood that hackers exploited a vulnerability in the software in order to extract certain member records, including information on outgoing payments. Up to 1.8 million individuals, representing more than half of all credit union members nationally, could potentially be affected.

Arguably, the most significant risk is targeted phishing. Since the stolen records contain authentic personal details, fraudulent communications are likely to appear considerably more credible, thereby increasing the probability that recipients will disclose confidential information.

The Data Protection Commission confirmed that it had received multiple breach notifications and was addressing the matter as a priority. Simultaneously, the Department of Finance is coordinating with the Central Bank, although a comprehensive assessment is contingent upon further information.
Credit unions will communicate with members directly where necessary, and Minister of State Robert Troy advised concerned members to seek clarification from their own credit union.
